title: SAEs on a grokked (a+b) mod 59 transformer: against a provable Fourier ground truth the raw neuron basis is 0.75 frequency-pure and the best usable SAE only 0.32 - the sparsity prior fights the density of the true features
hypothesis: A small overcomplete L1 sparse autoencoder trained on the MLP hidden activations of a fully grokked (a+b) mod 59 transformer will recover the model's known Fourier structure: a large fraction of its alive features will be frequency-pure (>=80% of their 2D Fourier power on a single frequency k) and the set of frequencies claimed by those features will match the model's key frequencies.
question: In the one interpretability setting with a PROVABLE answer key - a grokked modular-addition transformer, which is known to implement Fourier multiplication - do SAE features actually recover the ground-truth Fourier units, are all key frequencies recovered, and how does SAE faithfulness compare against the standard-basis (raw neuron) baseline that everyone skips?
method: No training of the task model: the fully grokked checkpoint (train acc 1.000, test acc 1.000, verified in-run at 1.0000 accuracy on all 3481 pairs) is LOADED from the sibling run 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition/model.pt, together with its saved key_freqs [24, 17, 5, 3, 6, 25]. Activation site: post-ReLU MLP hidden layer (d_mlp = 256) evaluated on ALL p^2 = 3481 inputs; activations are norm-scaled so E||x|| = sqrt(d) which makes the L1 coefficient comparable across models. SAE: standard ReLU dictionary (f = ReLU((x - b_dec) W_enc + b_enc), x_hat = f W_dec + b_dec), decoder rows renormalised to unit norm every step, L1 penalty on f, Adam lr 3e-3, batch 256, 2500 steps, dead-feature resampling at 40% and 70% of training. Arms: 4x expansion (1024 features) at three sparsity coefficients lambda in {0.3, 1.0, 3.0} on each of three activation sources, plus one extra 8x (2048-feature) grokked arm at lambda = 1.0 = 10 SAEs. GROUND-TRUTH SCORE: build the orthonormal real 2D Fourier basis over (a,b) in Z_59 x Z_59; frequency k's block is the 3x3 span {1, cos w_k a, sin w_k a} x {1, cos w_k b, sin w_k b} minus DC, and these blocks are disjoint once DC is dropped, so purity = max_k power_k / (total non-DC power) is a genuine partition statistic. A unit is PURE iff purity >= 0.8 and ALIVE iff it fires on >= 1% of the 3481 inputs. Two purity views per feature: (i) activation-map purity, the spectrum of the feature's own firing pattern f(a,b); (ii) decoder-direction purity, the spectrum of w_f . x(a,b) read out by the feature's unit-norm decoder direction - view (ii) ignores the ReLU gate and is deliberately the metric most favourable to the SAE. For a raw neuron the two coincide. FOUR CONTROLS: (1) the raw 256 MLP neurons scored with the identical metric (the head-to-head baseline); (2) SAEs on model_mid.pt, the memorized-not-generalizing checkpoint (test acc 0.102); (3) SAEs on a random-init transformer of the same architecture; (4) random-unit-direction and random-sparse-indicator-map nulls for the purity statistic itself. An arm is flagged COLLAPSED (and excluded from the headline, but still reported) if FVU > 0.25 or fewer than 10 features are alive, so that a dead autoencoder cannot claim a trivially perfect purity.
architecture: frozen 1-layer attention+MLP transformer, no LayerNorm, no biases, d_model 64 / 4 heads / d_mlp 256 / vocab 60, 56,960 params (loaded, not trained) + 10 ReLU sparse autoencoders, 4x (1024 feat, 0.53M params) and 8x (2048 feat, 1.05M params) over the 256-dim MLP hidden layer

dataset.name: MLP hidden activations of a grokked transformer on all 59^2 = 3481 (a,b) pairs of (a+b) mod 59; same for a memorized checkpoint and a random-init model
dataset.source: checkpoints from experiments/2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition (model.pt, model_mid.pt); inputs generated in run.py

task: sparse-dictionary recovery of a known ground-truth feature basis (Fourier features of a grokked modular-addition circuit)
compute: CPU single-threaded, 486.8s total (10 SAEs, 38-88s each) against a 640s training budget; no arm was skipped

metrics.reproducibility: two back-to-back runs produced identical results.json apart from per-arm wall-clock fields

result_summary: The hypothesis is REFUTED, and the sharpest number is the baseline nobody runs. Against a provable answer key, the RAW MLP NEURON BASIS of the grokked model is already 0.750 frequency-pure (mean purity 0.827, median 0.9257, 192 of 256 neurons pure) while the best NON-COLLAPSED SAE reaches only 0.318 (8x expansion, lambda=1.0) and the best 4x arm only 0.105. Even the deliberately SAE-friendly decoder-direction metric, which ignores the ReLU gate, peaks at 0.568 - still below the neurons. The SAE does not beat doing nothing. (2) SPARSITY IS THE CAUSE, AND THE PURE LIMIT IS DEGENERATE: purity rises monotonically with the L1 coefficient (0.120 -> 0.334 -> 0.917 mean) but so does FVU (0.009 -> 0.068 -> 0.990). The only arm that is 100% pure explains 1% of the variance with ONE surviving feature out of 1024 - a collapsed autoencoder, not an interpretation. Every arm that actually reconstructs is <= 0.32 pure. The mechanism is structural rather than a tuning failure: a true Fourier feature cos(w_k(a+b)) is DENSE (nonzero almost everywhere on the grid) while L1 rewards features that fire rarely - alive SAE features fire on 6.6-21.7% of inputs against 62.6% for the average neuron, and a localised indicator is spectrally broad by construction. The sparsity prior and the ground-truth feature shape are in direct conflict. (3) NO ARM RECOVERS THE KEY-FREQUENCY SET - BUT NEITHER DO THE NEURONS, AND THAT IS ITSELF A FINDING: the checkpoint's saved key_freqs (top-6 of the EMBEDDING spectrum) are {24, 17, 5, 3, 6, 25}, but the MLP layer only uses FOUR - all 192 pure neurons claim {3, 5, 17, 24}, holding 97.0% of neuron activation power, while freq 25 holds 0.65% and freq 6 holds 0.32%, less than frequency 11 which is not a key freq at all. So the embedding-derived key-frequency set OVER-COUNTS the algorithm the MLP actually runs by two, and any 'did the SAE find all key freqs' test inherits that. The best SAE arm claims a strict SUBSET, {5, 17, 24}, dropping frequency 3 entirely, with 0.911 of its dictionary dead. (4) CONTROLS ALL LAND WHERE THEY SHOULD: SAEs on the memorized-not-generalizing checkpoint are 0.000 pure at every lambda (max mean purity 0.092) and SAEs on a random-init transformer are 0.000 pure; raw neurons of those two models score 0.137 and 0.131 mean purity; random sparse indicator maps score 0.005. The metric is not 'any SAE looks pure' - the grokked model is the only source with recoverable structure and the SAE partially finds it. (5) A CAVEAT THAT CUTS AGAINST OUR OWN SAE-FRIENDLY METRIC: a RANDOM unit direction in the grokked activation space already scores 0.482 mean purity (p99 = 0.80), because that space is spanned by only 4 frequencies, so decoder-direction purity has a high null and the 0.638 mean at lambda=1.0 is a real but modest lift. The activation-map metric has a near-zero null (0.005) and is the honest one - and it is the metric on which the SAE does worst. CAVEATS, worst first: ONE SEED, one model, one site (MLP hidden; the post-attention residual stream was not swept, for budget); only 3 sparsity coefficients and 2 expansions; 2500 SAE steps on a fully-enumerated 3481-point dataset the SAE could in principle memorize; only the plain L1/ReLU SAE was tested, so this says nothing about top-k, JumpReLU or matryoshka variants that decouple L0 from per-feature density - which is exactly the mitigation the density mechanism predicts and the obvious next run; model_mid.pt comes from a different train/test split than model.pt (inherited from the sibling experiment), which does not affect its use here since activations are taken on all p^2 inputs; and the COLLAPSED-arm rule (FVU <= 0.25 and >= 10 alive) is a judgement call, fixed before purity was inspected.

novelty_check.conclusion: Partial prior art on every ingredient, none on the combination. The general claim that SAEs recover plausible-but-non-canonical units is the ICLR 2025 canonical-units critique (openreview HpUs2EXjOl, 'Rethinking Evaluation of Sparse Autoencoders'), listed in the backlog; the Fourier answer key and the frequency-purity style of neuron scoring are Nanda et al. 2301.05217; arXiv:2402.16726 analyses circuits in grokked transformers on modular polynomials but not with SAEs; the SAE recipe is Bricken et al. 'Towards Monosemanticity' / ARENA 3.1; and openreview DSOTgzeH3w ('On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy') gives theory that L1 SAEs are biased against high-density features, which is precisely the mechanism isolated empirically here. To our search, no prior work scores SAE features against the PROVABLE Fourier answer key of a grokked modular-addition transformer with (i) the raw neuron basis as a head-to-head baseline, (ii) memorized and random-init models as negative controls, and (iii) a random-direction null for the purity statistic itself. The three additions are the contribution - in particular the finding that the standard basis BEATS the learned dictionary (0.75 vs 0.32) and that the gap is explained by feature density rather than SAE tuning. The grokked model and the purity metric are replications. Search was web-only (arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this box); the two 2026-dated hits that surfaced were not leaned on for numbers.
